Southern Bahia, all Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo, Southeastern Minas Gerais, Eastern São Paulo, Northwestern Paraná and Eastern Santa Catarina in Brazil, Misiones in Argentina, probably also present in Northeastern Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil and in Southeastern Paraguay (Fig. 9). Habitat and natural history. Species associated to Atlantic forest from sea level to about 1300 m, also present in borders and small open areas surrounded by forest. A primarily coprophagous species, but with records from carcasses and rotten fruits. Diurnal, commonly found perching along forest trails. Very abundant species in all its range even in small forest patches.
